dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: SHARDFALL CITADEL — ARENA VAULT

dialogueInline.speaker: TRADE
dialogueInline.text: The manifests. Inspection access. Then the grain moves.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: It was inspected when it was loaded.

dialogueInline.speaker: TRADE
dialogueInline.text: By whom?

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: The growers. The carrier. The men and women whose names are on the freight bond.

dialogueInline.speaker: TRADE
dialogueInline.text: Verge names.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: Most of the grain is for Auric, yes. That was the arrangement before we stationed guns across their route. It hasn't become a different arrangement because you've become angry with it.

dialogueInline.speaker: TRADE
dialogueInline.text: You think I enjoy preventing food from reaching anyone?

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: I think you have eaten recently.

dialogueInline.speaker: TRADE
dialogueInline.text: Mind your manner.

panelPlan: SHARDFALL CITADEL — ARENA VAULT. The Trade Mask sits with a captain whose vessel has been held at the Gate picket. He has come wearing a work jacket with one.
The clerk glances up. Trade does not.
A movement among the guards. The captain doesn't look at them.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *SHARDFALL CITADEL — ARENA VAULT. The Trade Mask sits with a captain whose vessel has been held at the Gate picket. He has come wearing a work jacket with one sleeve freshly patched. A young clerk beside Trade turns the pages of a practical freight manifest. Nothing in the room is ceremonial except the fact that the people making the decision do not have to stand in the queue.*
*The clerk glances up. Trade does not.*
*A movement among the guards. The captain doesn't look at them.*

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: My crew's families live under the same roof your allocation officers use. We were supposed to receive a share from the return trade. Instead the cargo's sitting in a vacuum and I'm here asking permission to bring home a ship full of people who haven't been paid.

dialogueInline.speaker: TRADE
dialogueInline.text: That is precisely why the inspection must be recognized. If we surrender the registry now, we will be asking for every future shipment as a favor.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: The registry won't be much comfort to my youngest. She wants to know what we're having for supper.

dialogueInline.speaker: TRADE
dialogueInline.text: An effective negotiating position must last longer than a single meal.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: She's six. I'll try explaining long-term leverage. Perhaps she'll stop asking for bread.

panelPlan: Trade turns to the clerk.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Trade turns to the clerk.*

dialogueInline.speaker: TRADE
dialogueInline.text: The captain's berth remains registered. His crew will receive an allocation after inspection.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: What allocation?

dialogueInline.speaker: CLERK
dialogueInline.text: The amount hasn't been calculated.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: You see? Even your clerk won't make up a number for you. I'd hire her, if my ship were allowed to leave.

dialogueInline.speaker: TRADE
dialogueInline.text: You can return to the picket. Or relinquish your berth to a captain prepared to carry out its purpose.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: If you take the berth, you take the crew with it. That's what you keep forgetting. Those people were there when we welded it together. It isn't a chair you can give someone else.

dialogueInline.speaker: TRADE
dialogueInline.text: This audience is concluded.

dialogueInline.speaker: WORKER
dialogueInline.text: Did you get it?

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: No.

panelPlan: Trade's face remains concealed. The clerk lowers her head to the manifest.
The captain takes back his empty travel case. Outside, a worker who has waited the entire hearing asks if the freighter will come through tonight.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Trade's face remains concealed. The clerk lowers her head to the manifest.*
*The captain takes back his empty travel case. Outside, a worker who has waited the entire hearing asks if the freighter will come through tonight.*

dialogueInline.speaker: WORKER
dialogueInline.text: What did you tell them?

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: The truth, mostly.

dialogueInline.speaker: WORKER
dialogueInline.text: That was stupid.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: Evidently.

panelPlan: The worker goes back to the waiting crowd, furious. The captain stays for a moment. He knows the worker's family will go hungry before his own.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *The worker goes back to the waiting crowd, furious. The captain stays for a moment. He knows the worker's family will go hungry before his own.*

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: AURIC — GOVERNOR'S WORK ROOM

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: The first opening is narrower. Two food freighters can take it, provided neither captain gets adventurous. The second opens thirty minutes later. Medical transports have the better approach geometry there.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Food first. Medicine second.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: Would you like a moment to make that sound less dreadful?

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: The first ships can survive the narrow approach. The medical craft can't. We lose both loads if we swap them. I thought I might begin with the part that's true.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: Very brave. The families outside won't ask for a field calculation. They'll ask why the sick are waiting while a freighter full of grain goes first.

panelPlan: AURIC — GOVERNOR'S WORK ROOM. The air in the room is warm, though the adjoining hall is crowded with people who are not. Naomi has two independently verified.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *AURIC — GOVERNOR'S WORK ROOM. The air in the room is warm, though the adjoining hall is crowded with people who are not. Naomi has two independently verified reciprocal-field windows on the tactical plot, thirty minutes apart. Jex has brought his own crossing figures. Halev keeps rubbing his eyes and pretending he hasn't.*

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Then give them the calculation, Chris. Don't dress it up. The medical ships have less shear tolerance. It's not a judgment about which people you like better.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: I'll have the arrival teams explain it. Where do we berth the food ships?

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Where you told me you had room last week.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: We did have room last week.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: I've learned to treasure that expression. Usually it means somebody's turned a cargo floor into a bedroom.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Somebody did. Me.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: The merchants say you've been giving their docking reservations to people who don't pay.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: The people are paying. Just not with money I can put against the freight budget.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: A complicated way to run a city.

panelPlan: Jex tilts his head toward the closed door.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Jex tilts his head toward the closed door.*

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: You don't run cities.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I have the sense not to.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Neither window is a guarantee. We still have pickets across the approach. I can lead the first crossing. Tess will need a shield overlap for the second.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Will Fleet provide it?

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Deka can provide defensive cover within her order. I've spoken to her. She'll tell us exactly how much. I'm not asking her to promise the other ships will behave.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: I'll send out the current timing corrections. Publicly. Every pilot sees the same figures.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Including Billie.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: Including Billie. If I could arrange for information to be read only by people with charming personalities, I'd be a richer man than I already am.

panelPlan: Naomi taps her two timing marks.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Naomi taps her two timing marks.*

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: We wouldn't let you have the information.

dialogueInline.speaker: JEX
dialogueInline.text: See? That's why I like you.

dialogueInline.speaker: LIAISON
dialogueInline.text: They heard they're second.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Tell them why. You can use my name.

dialogueInline.speaker: LIAISON
dialogueInline.text: They already are.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Fair enough. Tell them I know thirty minutes is a very long time when it's somebody you love who's waiting.

panelPlan: Halev turns back to the arrival roster. A transport liaison enters. Her mother is on one of the medical ships.
She nods, not satisfied. Naomi heads for Sunlash. Jex leaves to publish updates rather than sell them. Halev remains to face the questions neither of them can.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: FLEET REVIEW ANNEX — DOCUMENT ROOM

dialogueInline.speaker: KEATING
dialogueInline.text: Before we begin, nobody in this room is reopening the order for the Gate screen. Deka has the assigned vessel. The civilian authorities have the windows they intend to use.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I wasn't going to challenge the crossing plan.

dialogueInline.speaker: KEATING
dialogueInline.text: You challenged two orders in one afternoon. My confidence in your intentions is not quite as robust as it once was.

dialogueInline.speaker: KERR
dialogueInline.text: We might save time by treating every sentence here as a proposal, not an order.

dialogueInline.speaker: KEATING
dialogueInline.text: That is precisely what I was going to suggest, Admiral. Without the air of discovery.

panelPlan: FLEET REVIEW ANNEX — DOCUMENT ROOM. Two civil Gate windows have already been publicly announced by Jex and Auric. The Shard pickets and each captain's choices.
The technician opens a recorded test. Two successive field readings disagree within a tolerable range; the verified transit boundary remains unchanged.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *FLEET REVIEW ANNEX — DOCUMENT ROOM. Two civil Gate windows have already been publicly announced by Jex and Auric. The Shard pickets and each captain's choices remain entirely outside Venn's control. Keating has agreed to let Venn attend a review of what Fleet's verification instruments are permitted to disclose to a civilian crossing authority. Kerr is there because he was willing to sign his name to the request. A technician has brought the relevant technical records, not a tactical display.*
*The technician opens a recorded test. Two successive field readings disagree within a tolerable range; the verified transit boundary remains unchanged.*

summary: THE PART YOU CAN MEASURE (INTERCUT AFTER SOURCE P03; NO CHANGE TO THE TWO-WINDOW PLAN) — 2/5

dialogueInline.speaker: TECHNICIAN
dialogueInline.text: What the civilians asked for is the instrument uncertainty and the test method. What the division asked me to release is a single certification mark. If I give them only the mark, they cannot tell when their older equipment has drifted.

dialogueInline.speaker: KEATING
dialogueInline.text: If you release the raw Fleet recordings, you may reveal where our survey vessels stand and what their instruments can observe.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Then remove the ship positions. Publish the tolerance band and the method used to arrive at it. Auric can compare against its own independent sensors.

dialogueInline.speaker: TECHNICIAN
dialogueInline.text: We can do that. It won't tell them where tonight's pickets are, and it won't tell anyone the full Fleet field track.

panelPlan: Continue the conversation at the established location; let the speakers’ changing reactions carry it.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceScene: NEW SCENE V6-A — THE PART YOU CAN MEASURE (INTERCUT AFTER SOURCE P03; NO CHANGE TO THE TWO-WINDOW PLAN)

summary: THE PART YOU CAN MEASURE (INTERCUT AFTER SOURCE P03; NO CHANGE TO THE TWO-WINDOW PLAN) — 3/5

dialogueInline.speaker: KERR
dialogueInline.text: Would it let a raider improve their timing?

dialogueInline.speaker: TECHNICIAN
dialogueInline.text: A raider can already read Jex's public updates. They might learn how little faith to put in an old sensor. The same is true of a freighter captain. The information has no conscience.

dialogueInline.speaker: KEATING
dialogueInline.text: A cheerful way to describe what you're proposing.

dialogueInline.speaker: TECHNICIAN
dialogueInline.text: I repair instruments, Admiral. The people who buy them supply the cheer.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: How long to validate this for civilian release?

dialogueInline.speaker: TECHNICIAN
dialogueInline.text: Long enough that the first crossing will be over. Probably the second too, if nobody asks me to rewrite every sentence for a committee.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Then don't pretend we're helping tonight's pilots. We're helping the next convoy determine whether the numbers they receive deserve to be believed.

panelPlan: Venn studies the tolerance band. The technician has marked a discrepancy in an instrument that was tested under load, not while a ship was in transit.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Venn studies the tolerance band. The technician has marked a discrepancy in an instrument that was tested under load, not while a ship was in transit.*

summary: THE PART YOU CAN MEASURE (INTERCUT AFTER SOURCE P03; NO CHANGE TO THE TWO-WINDOW PLAN) — 4/5

dialogueInline.speaker: KEATING
dialogueInline.text: You are suggesting that Fleet admit its instruments have limits.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: They've always had limits. We've been unusually fortunate that civilians haven't had the authority to read them.

dialogueInline.speaker: KERR
dialogueInline.text: That is not entirely fair.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: No. Neither is a certificate without a test method.

dialogueInline.speaker: KEATING
dialogueInline.text: Draft the stripped technical method and the uncertainty limits. Release it after validation. No vessel positions, no tactical observations, no names of informants or private crossings. Route the draft through the ordinary safety review, not Venn's correspondence file.

dialogueInline.speaker: TECHNICIAN
dialogueInline.text: Understood.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Thank you.

dialogueInline.speaker: KEATING
dialogueInline.text: I haven't given you a favor. I've authorized a defensible public standard.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I think I'm beginning to understand why those are different.

panelPlan: Keating turns to the technician.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Keating turns to the technician.*

summary: THE PART YOU CAN MEASURE (INTERCUT AFTER SOURCE P03; NO CHANGE TO THE TWO-WINDOW PLAN) — 5/5

dialogueInline.speaker: KEATING
dialogueInline.text: Good. Then perhaps we won't have to repeat this conversation when you find something else you want.

dialogueInline.speaker: KERR
dialogueInline.text: You could have asked her to release the whole recording.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: And spent another month arguing about why she couldn't. I used to have a ship to fill that month with work. I need to be more selective now.

dialogueInline.speaker: KERR
dialogueInline.text: That sounds dangerously like patience.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Don't tell anyone. They'll think I'm ill.

panelPlan: On the way out, Kerr pauses beside Venn.
The after-action technical release proceeds through a valid review. It cannot alter tonight's two crossings, which still depend on Halev's decision, Naomi's.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: THUNDERBREAK — COMMAND

dialogueInline.speaker: TACTICAL
dialogueInline.text: Shard transponders are going dark. The hulls haven't moved.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: How many?

dialogueInline.speaker: TACTICAL
dialogueInline.text: All the picket identifiers on the first screen. Second screen is following.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: Keep ours identified. Civilian pilots need to know where we are.

dialogueInline.speaker: TACTICAL
dialogueInline.text: Fleet control will call it a hostile concealment maneuver.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: It may be. It hasn't moved a ship one meter. Use the measured positions. Don't allow anyone to invent a fleet in an empty gap because a transponder stopped saying good morning.

dialogueInline.speaker: ENGINEERING
dialogueInline.text: Our port bus can cover the overlap, but I'd prefer to have it back before the second window. It's running warmer than I like.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: What do you like?

dialogueInline.speaker: ENGINEERING
dialogueInline.text: A functioning port bus.

panelPlan: THUNDERBREAK — COMMAND. Deka is in the captain's station. Her crew has been tracking real hulls, not trusting icons to substitute for sensor returns. Beyond.
An engineering officer approaches, irritated by the shield schedule.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *THUNDERBREAK — COMMAND. Deka is in the captain's station. Her crew has been tracking real hulls, not trusting icons to substitute for sensor returns. Beyond the cruiser, Shard pickets are stationary across both Gate approaches.*
*An engineering officer approaches, irritated by the shield schedule.*

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: A person of limited imagination. So am I.

dialogueInline.speaker: TACTICAL
dialogueInline.text: Gravefire wants yesterday's overlap.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: Hold it open for the skiffs. Their captain keeps the lead.

dialogueInline.speaker: TACTICAL
dialogueInline.text: She's still classified hostile in our registry.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: Then the registry can learn something from the viewports. She's carrying medical skiffs. The classification doesn't entitle us to drive the patients into a blockade.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: Ask engineering what the port bus can sustain for thirty minutes. Tell me the number they believe, not the number they'd give the Admiralty.

dialogueInline.speaker: ENGINEERING
dialogueInline.text: I heard that.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: Good. Saves a second message.

panelPlan: She studies the two openings. The first could be reached now. The second is barely more than a promise on the clocks.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *She studies the two openings. The first could be reached now. The second is barely more than a promise on the clocks.*

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTION
dialogueInline.text: SHARDFALL — ARENA VAULT

dialogueInline.speaker: TRADE
dialogueInline.text: Without recognized inspection, the medical convoy remains at the Gate.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: The pharmacists have inspected the cases. I've seen the seal numbers.

dialogueInline.speaker: TRADE
dialogueInline.text: We require the household lists. Recipient names. The shipborne custody sequence.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: You need to know whether the medicine is what the label says. You're asking to know where every person who needs it sleeps.

dialogueInline.speaker: TRADE
dialogueInline.text: Only those with something to conceal fear inspection.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: That's a wonderful system. The hungry produce a list of their children and the frightened tell you their addresses. Anyone who objects confesses to being guilty. Very efficient.

dialogueInline.speaker: RAID
dialogueInline.text: Gravefire will enforce the medical blockade.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: No.

dialogueInline.speaker: RAID
dialogueInline.text: You have a Gate-line posting, Captain. You may not choose which parts of the line you hold.

panelPlan: SHARDFALL — ARENA VAULT. Abby and Tess stand before Trade and Raid. A courier has brought the blocked medical manifest. The medicine is needed on Auric and in.
Abby turns slightly. Tess keeps looking at the masks.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *SHARDFALL — ARENA VAULT. Abby and Tess stand before Trade and Raid. A courier has brought the blocked medical manifest. The medicine is needed on Auric and in Shard settlements, including the place where one of Gravefire's mechanics lives.*
*Abby turns slightly. Tess keeps looking at the masks.*

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: I can choose what I do with my ship.

dialogueInline.speaker: RAID
dialogueInline.text: Then surrender the posting.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: That's done. Gravefire leaves with me.

dialogueInline.speaker: RAID
dialogueInline.text: The Confederacy made your command possible.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: My crew made it possible. The Confederacy helped us find a berth when the old yard broke apart. I haven't forgotten that. But you aren't taking the ship because I won't point her at medicine bound for our own families.

dialogueInline.speaker: TRADE
dialogueInline.text: You are making a long-term question into a personal grievance.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: One of the patients on that manifest patched my suit after Black Drift. She said if I ruined the cuff again she'd charge me double. Apparently I have a personal grievance with having her die before she can collect.

panelPlan: Trade speaks more gently than Raid.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Trade speaks more gently than Raid.*

dialogueInline.speaker: RAID
dialogueInline.text: This hearing has consequences beyond your affection for one patient.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Yes. I brought an entire ship to the hearing. I'm aware.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: Have you lost something?

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: My posting. I just spent a remarkably unpleasant ten minutes losing it.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: I meant why are you looking at your hands?

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: They were shaking. I'm checking if they've stopped.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: You should have warned me.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: What were you going to do, put your hand up and ask for a family recess?

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: I could have prepared the captains.

panelPlan: Raid has the attendant register the loss of Gate-line authority. Abby doesn't intervene. She knows doing so would imply Tess needs a superior captain to.
OUTSIDE THE VAULT. The air smells of hot metal. Tess stops at the threshold and appears to be counting her fingers.
Abby catches Tess's wrist. She has known those hands since they were children.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Raid has the attendant register the loss of Gate-line authority. Abby doesn't intervene. She knows doing so would imply Tess needs a superior captain to exercise a choice that is hers.*
*OUTSIDE THE VAULT. The air smells of hot metal. Tess stops at the threshold and appears to be counting her fingers.*
*Abby catches Tess's wrist. She has known those hands since they were children.*

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: We have thirty minutes between windows. If you can get seven of them to turn their guns aside, I'll get the skiffs through. Don't make them yours to order. Ask them.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: I know the difference.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: You know it when you're calm. You get very commanding when someone frightens you.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: I was frightened in there.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: So was I. There's something we can agree on.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: They'll take your berth next.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Probably. The crew's going to be furious. They were finally getting used to having a place where every other day didn't involve bargaining for cooling water.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: They could find another captain.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: They could. I wouldn't blame them.

panelPlan: Abby lets go of her wrist.
They watch a maintenance crew hurry past with an empty trolley, heading to prepare Gravefire's departure.
directionInline: Use supplied Rex Fleet references; retain scene continuity; exact scripted lettering only.
sourceActionBeats: *Abby lets go of her wrist.*
*They watch a maintenance crew hurry past with an empty trolley, heading to prepare Gravefire's departure.*

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: You would be unbearable about it for a month.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Two months. At least.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: Seven captains is not a vote I can win by standing in front of them and being right.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Good. You're learning. For years you've been so good at getting people to follow you that you forget sometimes they want to stay exactly where they are.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: They're risking the housing their crews worked for.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS

dialogueInline.speaker: FREIGHTER CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: Are you the one who said this opening was safe?

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: No. I'm the one who said we could use it if you listened.

dialogueInline.speaker: FREIGHTER CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: That's not how it was repeated to me.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: I'll take that up with my publicity department. It's a very small department.

dialogueInline.speaker: SECOND
dialogueInline.text: She is her publicity department.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: And as you can see, I do an appalling job.

dialogueInline.speaker: FREIGHTER CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: Can I follow you exactly?

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Follow the published fixes and your own instruments. If you put your ship where I was thirty seconds ago, you'll be late to a very different piece of space.

dialogueInline.speaker: SECOND
dialogueInline.text: First window settling.

sourceActionBeats: *VEIL MARKET — HANGAR. Sunlash is ready. Two working freighters hold grain for Auric. Their captains have been watching the Gate measurements and one another for so long that irritation has replaced anxiety.*

*Naomi goes through the approach once more: Sunlash leads, food freighters staggered, no sudden burns near the anchor marker. The physics are measurable and unforgiving. These aren't doors opened by magic; they're volumes whose reciprocal-field tolerances are known for short periods.*

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Then let's stop talking about it.

dialogueInline.speaker: SECOND
dialogueInline.text: Freighter Two struck the marker. Mast damage. Their pilot wants to turn back.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: Tell them not to. The geometry they're in will carry them out if they keep their present burn. A rescue turn puts them across the other freighter's bow.

dialogueInline.speaker: FREIGHTER CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: I can't keep my mast upright.

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: You don't need to. You need to keep your ship upright.

dialogueInline.speaker: FREIGHTER CAPTAIN
dialogueInline.text: Is that supposed to be comforting?

dialogueInline.speaker: NAOMI
dialogueInline.text: It's supposed to be an instruction.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Can it unload?

dialogueInline.speaker: DOCK SUPERVISOR
dialogueInline.text: Yes. Slowly. The mast's in the way, and I won't put anyone underneath it until it's braced.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: Then start on the undamaged ship. Tell the queue exactly which grain is available tonight.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOCK SUPERVISOR
dialogueInline.text: They'll complain we promised more.

dialogueInline.speaker: HALEV
dialogueInline.text: We did promise more. They should complain. That doesn't mean we tell them the rest has arrived before it can be unloaded.

dialogueInline.speaker: EMISSARY
dialogueInline.text: The loyalist relief force is still thirty minutes out. We cannot reposition before the medical window.

dialogueInline.speaker: TRADE
dialogueInline.text: Then instruct the existing captains to maintain their obstruction. The Gate cannot be left to whoever arrives with medicine and a persuasive story.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: I can route it under your authority.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: That's the one thing you mustn't do. These ships don't belong to me.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: They know you. Some of them would obey.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: Yes. And after tonight we'd be explaining why a favor became an order. Send requests. One to each captain.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN ONE
dialogueInline.text: Raid will freeze my berth.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: He may.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN ONE
dialogueInline.text: That means my crew's families are out of heated quarters.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: I can offer repair time on Scythe's outer rail, while we have it. I cannot give you housing. I'm not going to pretend the two are the same.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: Have you decided?

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN ONE
dialogueInline.text: Don't rush me. I'm trying to think of one worse.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN TWO
dialogueInline.text: You want us to rotate weapons off the medical lane. What happens if a loyalist fires from behind us?

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: You keep the right to defend your crew. I'm asking you not to shoot at civilians or close the route. You decide when the line is no longer defensible.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN TWO
dialogueInline.text: So we risk being branded traitors and you still won't promise protection.

panelPlan: SECOND CALL.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: I can promise you accurate positions. I can promise I won't claim you joined my command. I cannot promise nobody will shoot at you.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN THREE
dialogueInline.text: No. I lost one berth following promises about where the supplies would go. My crew's not paying for your conscience.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: Understood.

dialogueInline.speaker: OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: You're not going to try him again?

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: No. He said no. We're allowed to hear that.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN FOUR
dialogueInline.text: We will rotate off the medical lane. We are not joining a new fleet. And I want that said while people are listening.

dialogueInline.speaker: ABBY
dialogueInline.text: I will say it.

dialogueInline.speaker: CAPTAIN FOUR
dialogueInline.text: Good. Because everyone seems to think whoever has the best timing chart gets to own the ships using it.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA
dialogueInline.text: You'll have to, Captain. My engineering officer is threatening to take my chair away if I warm the port bus another degree.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: I'd listen to the engineer. They usually know where the fire starts.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASHFANG OFFICER
dialogueInline.text: Our reserves won't support a fight.

dialogueInline.text: Then don't start one.

dialogueInline.speaker: LOYALIST CAPTAIN

dialogueInline.text: We aren't particularly expensive anymore.

dialogueInline.speaker: BILLIE
dialogueInline.text: It cost me enough. I am not having an argument about market value while somebody is aiming weapons at our tail.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Medical Two, I see the turn. Stop it. You're not in trouble for being frightened. You will be in trouble if you put your patients in the shear because you want to get away from someone else's guns.

dialogueInline.text: I can't see the marker.

dialogueInline.speaker: TESS
dialogueInline.text: Then use my hull as your reference. Stay on the inside of my wake. Don't invent a new route because you don't like the view.

dialogueInline.text: Both crossings clear. The food freighter needs a hull team. No weapons fire.

dialogueInline.speaker: DEKA

dialogueInline.text: Thank you, Janet. That improves my mood enormously.

dialogueInline.speaker: KERR
dialogueInline.text: He prefers a simple story.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: I prefer knowing when a Commodore has been removed from command and is no longer quietly building a small foreign ministry from a review cabin.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I haven't been directing any of those people. Naomi has reminded me of that with exceptional clarity.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: Yet they answer your calls.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Sometimes. Many don't. One asked me not to call again. Another sent an invoice simply for speaking to me.

dialogueInline.speaker: KERR
dialogueInline.text: Did you pay it?

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: It was a very good invoice. I considered keeping it.

panelPlan: Even Keating's mouth moves a fraction. Dominion doesn't surrender the room to the joke.

summary: A JOB THAT DOESN'T GIVE HER A SHIP (AFTER SOURCE P16; LEADS INTO ISSUE 7) — 3/7
settingText: BASTION SPIRE — SMALL FLEET CONFERENCE ROOM

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: We have a problem. Fleet's next survey group needs shared observations from independent pilots. Those pilots won't submit their civilian traffic to Fleet. The Shard captains won't accept Admiralty instructions. Meanwhile every fresh corridor discrepancy becomes an argument about who owns the route.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: You need a place where the measurements can be compared without any one side claiming the others have accepted its authority.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: Yes. And I need a Fleet officer whose presence doesn't turn that place into a surrender negotiation.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: There are several competent people who could do the work.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: You've spoken to most of them. They all suggested someone else.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I see.

summary: A JOB THAT DOESN'T GIVE HER A SHIP (AFTER SOURCE P16; LEADS INTO ISSUE 7) — 4/7
settingText: BASTION SPIRE — SMALL FLEET CONFERENCE ROOM

dialogueInline.speaker: KEATING
dialogueInline.text: The tribunal finding remains in force. I will oppose anything that makes this an indirect reinstatement to *Thunderbreak*.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: So will I. Lieutenant Deka commands the cruiser. Nothing about the assignment changes her authority over its crew, handling, weapons, or engineering limits.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: And no authority over Auric's traffic, Naomi's pilots, or the Shard captains.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: Correct. You may coordinate the participating Fleet task-group reports within an approved corridor operation, seek consent to share observations, and recommend deconfliction measures. You cannot promise another faction protection beyond the forces actually assigned. You cannot order a civilian vessel. You cannot reclaim a ship because you used to know its captain.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: You make it sound almost unattractive.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: It's not a reward, Ella.

panelPlan: There is an old familiarity in the use of her first name. Keating looks from one to the other but says nothing.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Does Deka know you intend to put me on her bridge?

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: I've requested her ship as the Fleet coordination platform. I have not yet received her assessment of the operational impact.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Then don't announce anything until she has a chance to object. She has earned command. If the first thing I do is stand behind her chair while the crew waits for me to nod, we'll be worse off than when you called me.

dialogueInline.speaker: KERR
dialogueInline.text: Is that your condition?

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: It's a condition of making the arrangement useful. I don't need a chair. I need somewhere the different accounts can reach one another.

dialogueInline.speaker: KEATING
dialogueInline.text: And if Deka refuses to host you?

summary: A JOB THAT DOESN'T GIVE HER A SHIP (AFTER SOURCE P16; LEADS INTO ISSUE 7) — 6/7
settingText: BASTION SPIRE — SMALL FLEET CONFERENCE ROOM

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Then use another platform. Or let her suggest one. She has the ship. I don't.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: You'll still answer to Fleet for your conduct. The temporary authorization will expire with the defined task group. No restoration of ordinary fleet command, no change to the disciplinary record.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I understand.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: You once told me you couldn't do your duty without a ship.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Did I?

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: You were younger. I was hoping the age had made you less certain.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: It has made me more aware of how many people can say no. I don't think that's a weakness anymore.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: Don't be too pleased with yourself. We're still going to argue about every practical limit.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I'd have been disappointed otherwise.

panelPlan: Dominion studies Venn for a long moment. He had expected a request for restoration, perhaps a grievance. She has offered to make herself inconvenient.
Keating reaches for the authorization draft. Venn stops her, almost instinctively.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: One more line. Please. When the Fleet task group issues a shared report, the underlying observations must remain attributed to the people and vessels that supplied them, subject to their consent and safety. Fleet can't turn a Shard captain's reading into a Fleet achievement just because we have the better printing equipment.

dialogueInline.speaker: KEATING
dialogueInline.text: That's not operational authority. It's records practice.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: I know. It's what we have been arguing about since the first rescue.

dialogueInline.speaker: DOMINION
dialogueInline.text: For a considerable portion of my life, it feels like.

dialogueInline.speaker: KEATING
dialogueInline.text: I'll draft the condition. I won't guarantee the other parties like it.

dialogueInline.speaker: VENN
dialogueInline.text: Neither will I.

sourceActionBeats: *The meeting ends without reinstatement or celebration. In the corridor Venn receives one short message from the liaison office: Deka has asked for the written scope before agreeing to host the coordination station. She hasn't accepted yet. Venn reads it, puts away her old insignia case, and returns to her room to write a reply that begins not with instructions, but with a request.*
